name: Evolving ambient bed from a captured micro-loop: two parallel band-pass lanes swept by unsynchronised slow LFOs, delays on each lane, an octave-down lane, all summed into a bus with a very slow, also unsynchronised auto-pan
goal: Turn a short played loop (guitar or any instrument captured in a micro-looper) into an organic, never-repeating ambient backing pad. Two parallel (not series) narrow band-pass filters each let through a small wedge of the spectrum ('a flashlight on a painting') and sweep slowly up and down at different, unsynchronised rates. Each lane runs through a delay, one lane also gets an octave-down effect, and both feed a third bus with a very slow auto-pan that is unsynchronised with both filters, so three out-of-time movements create endless variation. Delta vs the generative/noodle-wind variants: an audio-loop source (not noise) with two async band-pass lanes, an octave-down lane and an async auto-pan bus.

source.title: The Joy of Recording Episode 1: Evolving Ambient Textures

prerequisites: A looper or sampler to capture a short loop
Two band-pass filters with free-running (Hz, not synced) LFOs
Delay, octave-down pitch effect, auto-pan, reverb

inputs.name: micro_loop
inputs.description: Short loop of played material (guitar, keys, etc.)

outputs.name: texture_bed
outputs.description: Evolving ambient bed usable as a piece or as a backing pad to write over

constraints: The transcript gives no numeric rates; choose slow, mutually unrelated free-running rates for the two filter LFOs and the auto-pan (avoid simple ratios so they never line up).
Movement is filter, delay and pan only; the octave-down lane is a fixed -12 st, so pitch stays steady (Matt's preference).
Keep delay feedback moderate so repeats smear rather than tick (no rapid clicking texture).
If the track has drums, they enter early (~8 counts / ~12 s); only pad/texture before that (Matt's preference).
Ableton/MIDI-friendly: device names map to stock Live devices or generic modules; patterns are plain MIDI clips.

Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with Ableton, Reason, Bitwig, Soundtoys, FabFilter, Eventide or any vendor. Map product devices to generic modules (sampler, noise osc, filter, envelope, LFO, EQ, saturator, compressor, delay, reverb) in any DAW, hardware or Web Audio.
Steady pitch: no random pitch wobble or randomised notes; no rapid clicking textures (Matt's preference).

steps.action: Capture a small loop of played material in a micro-looper or sampler as the source nugget.
Send it to two parallel lanes (side by side, not one into the other), each with a narrow band-pass filter that passes only a small wedge of the spectrum.
steps.expect: Two thin, different slices of the loop

steps.action: Sweep each band-pass slowly up and down the spectrum with its own free-running LFO at a different, unsynchronised rate.
steps.expect: Slices reveal different frequencies at different times

steps.action: Put a delay on each lane; on one lane also add an octave-down effect to extend the range downward.
steps.expect: Wider 'sonic orchestra' with a lower register

steps.action: Route both lanes into a third bus with a very slow auto-pan whose rate is unrelated to both filter LFOs; add reverb.
steps.expect: Three out-of-time movements; the texture never repeats exactly

steps.action: Render a long take and use it as an ambient piece or as a bed to play grooves and melodies over.

verification: Spectral centroid of the rendered bed varies slowly over time with no exact repeat at the source loop length.
Pan position cycles slower than either filter sweep.
No pitch movement except the fixed octave-down layer.
